subject: Karen's Window Watcher — a small freeware Windows utility written in Visual Basic 6.0 by Karen Kenworthy
subject_category: simple utility (system inspection: lists every top-level and child window of every running program, including hidden windows)

original_publication_date.basis: Origin server Last-Modified header preserved by the archive: 'Wed, 03 Sep 2003 13:22:03 GMT'. The earliest archived copy of this exact file is 2003-09-17. This is the file's modification date on karenware.com, not proof of first public posting.

depicted_event_date.basis: The program's own status bar in the image reads '9/3/2003' and '8:19 AM' (the capturing computer's clock at capture time).
depicted_event_date.note: Separate from the program's first release. Window Watcher was introduced in Karen's Power Tools newsletter dated September 28, 1999 (archived copy stored), so the image shows a 2003 build of a 1999 VB6 utility.

basis: The Explorer-like tree view is the interface the 2003 page credits to version 2.0.
The 'Locate' button matches the version 2.1 change 'Can now display on-screen location of selected windows'.
The file's Last-Modified date (2003-09-03) precedes the v2.2.1 page update (Sep 23, 2003), so the build shown may be 2.1 or 2.2; no version number is visible in the image.
version_model_evidence.operating_system_shown: Windows XP-style (Luna) window frame and controls; module path C:\WINDOWS\System32. Inferred from appearance; no OS version string is visible.
version_model_evidence.vb_version_evidence_in_image: The selected child window is the program's own 'Find Next' button. Its details read 'Module File Name: C:\WINDOWS\System32\MSVBVM60.DLL' (the Visual Basic 6.0 runtime library) and 'Class Name: ThunderRT6CommandButton' (the window class of a command button in a compiled VB6 program).

vb_provenance_evidence.source: Karen's Power Tools Newsletter, September 28, 1999, by Karen Kenworthy
vb_provenance_evidence.evidence: Offers the program's Visual Basic 6.0 source code; separately notes the Visual Basic Runtime v6.0 is required by all the Power Tools.

vb_provenance_evidence.class_name_reference: VB6 intrinsic controls use proprietary 'ThunderRT6…' window classes in compiled programs. See O'Reilly, 'Subclassing and Hooking with Visual Basic', ch. 7 'How the Superclassing Example Works' (https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/subclassing-and-hooking/0596001185/ch07s02.html), located by search on 2026-09-15; the page text was not stored. Treat as secondary support only.
